To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystalline silicates are found in the hot dust close to the central star, as well as in the colder dust in the outer disk, that there are both small and large crystalline grains, and that the crystalline fraction is higher than 15%, but less than 33%.

we discovered the first very low mass object with a circum(sub)-stellar disk with a very high crystalline silicate fraction, and that this object shows evidence for combined grain settling and growth in the disk.

the first very low mass star with a crystalline silicates feature in the Spitzer IRS spectrum has a disk with a high fraction of crystalline silicates, that the crystalline fraction is comparable for the small and large grains and for the hot and cold dust, that the small and large dust grains are mixed, and that the dust is settling in the disk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of stars and planetary systems.
the formation and evolution of the dust in the circumstellar disks around young stellar objects.
the formation and evolution of the dust grains in the disks around very low mass stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystalline silicates are formed at the inner edge of the disk and are subsequently transported to the outer edge by radial mixing.

the crystalline silicates are formed by grain growth in the inner disk, followed by radial mixing to the outer disk, and that the crystalline mass fraction in the inner disk is at least a factor of 2 higher than in the outer disk.
the crystalline silicate mass fraction of the total dust mass in the disk of SST-Lup-3-1 is in the range 15%-33% and that it is a combination of large and small grains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disk of the very low mass star SST-Lup3 is rich in dust grains, and the dust is rich in crystalline silicates.
this is a very low mass object with an unusually rich disk.
crystalline silicates are present at all temperatures in the disk of SST-Lup-3-1, and that grain growth and settling are both present in this very low mass star's disk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallinity is not only high but also that it is distributed over a wide temperature range, and that it is not only present in the hot, inner part of the disk but also in the cold outer disk.
even in very small disks, the dust composition is not uniform, and that crystalline silicates are not restricted to the outer parts of disks.
crystalline silicates can form in the disks of low-mass young stellar objects.
